explanation: The king of Judah who urged the people to turn back to God and righteousness.
Individuals appointed by Josaphat to judge fairly and impartially in accordance with God's laws.
A reverent awe and respect for God, leading to obedience to His commands and a rejection of evil.
The process of restoring and improving religious practices and beliefs so that they align more closely with God's will.
Members of the tribe of Levi who held special religious roles and responsibilities in ancient Israel.
The supreme religious leader in ancient Israel, responsible for performing sacrifices and other ceremonies in the temple.
A priest and prophet during King Josaphat's reign who gave counsel and guidance according to God's word.
Agreement with reality or actual events; in this context, it also means being faithful to God's commands.
Doing something with full effort and commitment, without reservation or half-heartedness.
